## Experiment

Repeat of the `coop --git` step-counter baseline (`coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash_10-stepcounter`, 8/10) run on Vertex AI at `-c 10` with a `$40` per-agent cost cap (`gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K) to verify Vertex AI parity with zero rate-limit retries before running communication ablations.

## Observations

- 9/10 passed (within 1 pair of the 8/10 AI Studio run `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash_10-stepcounter`), with `$11.57` cost, 64-minute wall time (down from 83 minutes at `-c 4`), and zero API retries at 2.07M input tokens/min peak load.
- Zero merge conflicts across all 10 pairs (9 `clean` merges and 1 `identical` patch on `typst_task/6554`); `go_chi_task/26`, which conflicted in the first run, merged cleanly and passed after 48 messages between the peers.
- All 20 of 20 agents pushed patches (including `dspy_task/8394` `agent2`, which did not open a PR before hitting step 100 so grading fell back to its pushed branch). The lone failure, `pillow_task/290` (feature 4 failed, feature 5 passed after a clean merge), also fails in 250-step `solo` — leaving essentially zero coordination-failure headroom left on `flash_10` for `gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking (unlike the harder `core` subset at 4/10).
- Agents sent 250 messages total (25.0 per pair).
